subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should this issue be resolved by making live gateway memory-runtime health the source of truth for status, or is the current `not checked` behavior sufficient for normal/deep status?
rationale: Current main avoids the old wording but does not implement the requested live-runtime health contract, and the open conflicting fork PR plus the broader status side-effect issue need one owner-chosen direction.

options.title: Use the broader live-gateway contract
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 the canonical implementation path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Revive the fork PR
options.body: Ask the fork PR author to rebase, resolve conflicts, and prove `status --deep` plus JSON status against a real external memory plugin without local plugin side effects.

options.title: Accept `not checked` as sufficient
options.body: Declare the shipped wording sufficient, close the conflicting fork PR, and close this issue with release evidence.

recommendation.title: Use the broader live-gateway contract
recommendation.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 the canonical implementation path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame and the original memory-runtime routing history put the central status/plugin-runtime boundary under Peter Steinberger's recent work.
